title: optimize-cpu-request-path-thread-pinning-serialization-continuous-batching
author: Aisha Patel
release_notes: Reduced CPU-path tail latency by ~15-25% and lowered p99 CPU utilization for small requests by addressing serialization hotspots and improving thread-pool pinning and scheduling.
description:
Summary:
This PR addresses CPU-side bottlenecks observed in the serving runtime for mixed CPU/GPU deployments and pure-CPU nodes. Root causes identified: heavy request serialization overhead, contention in the generic thread pool, and suboptimal CPU affinity for per-worker thread-pools which amplified context-switching under load. The change set reduces serialization allocations, introduces a dedicated request-thread-pool with CPU pinning options, and optimizes the scheduling path for short/latency-sensitive requests to improve continuous batching latency profiles.

Motivation & Context:
- Internal benchmarks (ENG-2174) showed p95/p99 latency regressions on small prompt workloads when KV cache hits are common and GPU is busy; CPU-side scheduling dominated tail latency.
- Related incidents: INT-4432 (Feb 10) where a small regression in host-side scheduling caused elevated tail latency during traffic spikes.
- Goal: reduce request-processing overhead and variance without changing model kernels or GPU scheduling; make improvements configurable and guarded behind runtime flags.

What changed (high level):
- Introduced a dedicated RequestWorkerPool (runtime/request_pool) separate from the global worker pool for short-lived request tasks to avoid starvation and large-task contention.
- Added optional CPU affinity (pinning) for RequestWorkerPool threads; default is enabled on linux for dedicated-serving nodes.
- Rewrote the request serialization path to use a preallocated buffer pool and span-based encoders to remove multiple allocations per request (runtime/serialize).
- Fast-path for KV-cache hits: bypass additional copy when request surface is <= 4KB and no client-side transforms are required.
- Adjusted batching scheduler heuristics: prefer dispatch to pinned-request-pool when estimated latency < 50ms to reduce context switches.
- New metrics: request_pool_queue_depth, request_pool_worker_affinity, serialization_allocs_removed.

Commits (summary):
- 8a4c1f0: add RequestWorkerPool with basic lifecycle and tests
- c3b9d4e: implement cpu affinity flags + system detection on linux
- 1f7b2e2: replace serializer with span-encoder + buffer pool; add benchmarks
- d9e2c66: batching scheduler: prefer short-request routing to request pool
- f45b9aa: add observability hooks and dashboards + docs
- a11d3b1: e2e perf tests and flamegraph artifacts for CI

Files changed (high level):
- runtime/request_pool.h/.cc: new pool implementation and affinity options
- runtime/serialize.h/.cc: span-encoder, buffer-pool, removed legacy encoders
- runtime/batching/scheduler.cc: routing heuristics to new pool
- docs/perf/README.md: guidance on enabling pinning and tuning pool size
- metrics/metrics_registry.yaml: new metric definitions
- tests/perf/request_pool_perf_test.cc: microbenchmarks and regression asserts

Benchmarks & results:
- Local perf harness (mixed CPU/GPU, 32 clients, 1000qps) before/after:
  - median latency: 14.3ms -> 12.1ms (15% improvement)
  - p95 latency: 52ms -> 41ms (21% improvement)
  - p99 latency: 120ms -> 93ms (22.5% improvement)
  - CPU p99 utilization on host threads: 78% -> 62%
- Continuous batching traces show fewer preemption spikes and reduced KV-cache hit dispatch overhead.

Testing done:
- Unit tests for RequestWorkerPool lifecycle and affinity behavior
- Serializer microbenchmarks and regression tests validating zero-copy fast-path for small requests
- Integration cluster run (canary) against internal traffic profile: 72-hour run with metrics validated against regression thresholds in ENG-2174
- CI: linux/clang and linux/gcc build + perf-test stage. A flaky perf test failed on first CI run (timeout when collecting flamegraph) and was retriggered; final status: pass.

Review conversation (high level):
- Marco Nguyen: "Can you make pool size autoscale based on queue depth? Also we should ensure the pinning flag defaults to off for non-dedicated nodes."
  - Aisha: "Added adaptive sizing based on 95th queue latency and made pinning default-on only for nodes with label 'dedicated-serving=true'. See runtime/request_pool.cc line 184 for heuristics."
- Elena Kovács: "Serializer change looks good; please add a fallback to the legacy path for older ABI builds."
  - Aisha: "Added compatibility layer and unit test; legacy encoder retained under a feature flag in runtime/serialize_compat.h."
- Rajat Singh: "Please provide a short doc in docs/perf on when to enable pinning and SRE runbook to roll back if CPU hotspots observed."
  - Aisha: "Added docs/perf/README.md and an SRE checklist for rollback. Included CPU counters and suggested thresholds."

CI Summary:
- Build: pass (linux/clang, linux/gcc)
- Unit tests: pass
- Perf-stage: initial run had a flaky timeout when collecting flamegraph (infra), retried and passed; artifacts attached (flamegraphs and perf results)
- E2E canary: passed internal gating (72h)

Migration and flags:
- New runtime flags: --request-pool-enabled, --request-pool-size, --request-pool-pin, --request-serializer-fastpath-enable
- Defaults: request-pool enabled on all nodes, pinning enabled only on nodes labeled dedicated-serving=true to avoid surprising behavior on multi-tenant nodes.

Operational notes:
- Added Grafana panels for request_pool_queue_depth and serialization_allocs_removed. Query examples in docs/perf/README.md.
- SRE rollback steps: set --request-pool-enabled=false and restart runtime (graceful drain available).

Follow-ups (tracked):
- ENG-2190: extend adaptive autosizing to consider CPU/headroom signals from node exporter
- ENG-2191: upstream serializer improvements to support streaming encoders and reduce end-to-end latency further

Merge details:
- Merge method: squash and merge
- Merged by: Marco Nguyen after approvals from Elena and Rajat
